name: button
title: Button
description: Displays a button or a component that looks like a button.
accessibilityNotes: Renders a native `<button>` by default, or a native `<a>` when `href` is passed (see `packages/shadcn/ui/button/button.marko`) — either way the element is a real interactive element, so it is keyboard-activatable with `Enter` and `Space` (`<a>`: `Enter` only, following the link) and reachable by `Tab` for free — no custom key handling or ARIA role is added.

`disabled` is the native `<button>` attribute, passed straight through via `...rest` — it removes the button from the tab order and blocks pointer and keyboard activation, matching every other native form control. The `variants.ts` styles (`disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50`) key off that same native state rather than a separate `data-disabled` flag.

Pass `href` and `Button` renders an `<a>` with the same styling and data attributes — the Marko equivalent of shadcn's `asChild`. There is no `render`/`asChild` prop (unlike upstream Base UI's `Button`, whose polymorphic `render` prop still applies `role="button"` and overrides the `<a>`'s native link semantics); the anchor keeps its native link role and keyboard behavior instead of inheriting button semantics. To style markup `Button` does not wrap, apply the `buttonVariants` helper directly to it.

examples.title: Button Group
examples.source:
import ButtonGroup from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/button-group/button-group.marko";
import Button from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/button/button.marko";
import DropdownMenu from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.marko";
import Icon from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/icon/icon.marko";

static const LABEL_ITEMS = [
  { value: "personal", label: "Personal" },
  { value: "work", label: "Work" },
  { value: "other", label: "Other" },
];

<ButtonGroup>
  <ButtonGroup class="hidden sm:flex">
    <Button type="button" variant="outline" size="icon" aria-label="Go Back">
      <Icon name="ArrowLeft"/>
    </Button>
  </ButtonGroup>
  <ButtonGroup>
    <Button type="button" variant="outline">Archive</Button>
    <Button type="button" variant="outline">Report</Button>
  </ButtonGroup>
  <ButtonGroup>
    <Button type="button" variant="outline">Snooze</Button>
    <DropdownMenu>
      <@trigger|triggerProps|>
        <Button type="button" variant="outline" size="icon" aria-label="More Options" ...triggerProps>
          <Icon name="MoreHorizontal"/>
        </Button>
      </@trigger>
      <@item value="mark-read">
        <Icon name="Mail" data-icon="inline-start"/> Mark as Read
      </@item>
      <@item value="archive">
        <Icon name="ArchiveIcon" data-icon="inline-start"/> Archive
      </@item>
      <@item type="separator"/>
      <@item value="snooze">
        <Icon name="ClockIcon" data-icon="inline-start"/> Snooze
      </@item>
      <@item value="add-calendar">
        <Icon name="Calendar" data-icon="inline-start"/> Add to Calendar
      </@item>
      <@item value="add-list">
        <Icon name="ListIcon" data-icon="inline-start"/> Add to List
      </@item>
      <@item type="sub" label="Label As..." subEntries=LABEL_ITEMS/>
      <@item type="separator"/>
      <@item value="trash" variant="destructive">
        <Icon name="Trash2Icon" data-icon="inline-start"/> Trash
      </@item>
    </DropdownMenu>
  </ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.description: Use `ButtonGroup` to group related buttons together. See the Button Group documentation for more details.

examples.title: As Link
examples.source:
import Button from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/button/button.marko";

<Button href="#" variant="secondary" size="sm">
  Login
</Button>
examples.description: Pass `href` to render an `<a>` with the same styling — the Marko equivalent of shadcn's `asChild`. The element stays a real anchor (no `role="button"` override), so middle-click, "copy link address" and keyboard activation all behave natively. `buttonVariants` is still available when you need the classes on markup you control yourself.

examples.description: `disabled` is a native `<button>` attribute — it passes straight through to the element.
